arxiv-2103-11035.title: Modeling Coral Reef Bleaching Recovery Through KCC-Theory
arxiv-2103-11035.creator: Rafael Cavalcanti, Solange Rutz
arxiv-2103-11035.description: Abstract We use Volterra-Hamilton systems theory and their associated cost functional to study the population dynamics and productive processes of coral reefs in recovery from bleaching and show that the cost of production remains the same after the process. The KCC-theory geometrical invariants are determined for the model proposed to describe the renewed symbiotic interaction between coral and algae.

arxiv-2104-15076.title: Climate Modelling in Low-Precision: Effects of both Deterministic & Stochastic Rounding.
arxiv-2104-15076.creator: E. Adam Paxton, Matthew Chantry, Milan Klöwer, Leo Saffin & Tim Palmer
arxiv-2104-15076.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by E. Adam Paxton, Matthew Chantry, Milan Klöwer, Leo Saffin & Tim Palmer. Motivated by recent advances in operational weather forecasting, we study the efficacy of low-precision arithmetic for climate simulations. We develop a framework to measure rounding error in a climate model which provides a stress-test for a low-precision version of the model, and we apply our method to a variety of models including the Lorenz system; a shallow water approximation for turbulent flow over a ridge; and a coarse resolution global atmospheric model

arxiv-2105-04105.title: On the Hardness of Opinion Dynamics Optimization with L 1 L_{1} -Budget on Varying Susceptibility to Persuasion
arxiv-2105-04105.creator: T-H. Hubert Chan, Chui Shan Lee
arxiv-2105-04105.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by T-H. Hubert Chan, Chui Shan Lee. Recently, Abebe et al. (KDD 2018) and Chan et al. (WWW 2019) have considered an opinion dynamics optimization problem that is based on a popular model for social opinion dynamics, in which each agent has some fixed innate opinion, and a resistance that measures the importance it places on its innate opinion; moreover, the agents influence one another’s opinions through an iterative process. Under certain conditions, this iterative process converges to some equilibrium opinion vector.

arxiv-2209-08528.title: Canonical diagonal liftings I: dormant PGL n \mathrm{PGL}_{n} -opers on algebraic curves
arxiv-2209-08528.creator: Yasuhiro Wakabayashi
arxiv-2209-08528.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yasuhiro Wakabayashi. The present paper forms the first part of a series in which we treat some topics on dormant opers and Frobenius-Ehresmann structures from an arithmetic point of view. In the present paper, motivated by the issue of lifting homogeneous linear differential equations in prime characteristic p p , we generalize the moduli theory of dormant PGL n \mathrm{PGL}_{n} -opers on pointed stable curves.

arxiv-2301-01373.title: Covariate-Guided Bayesian Mixture of Spline Experts for the Analysis of Multivariate Time Series
arxiv-2301-01373.creator: Haoyi Fu, Lu Tang, Ori Rosen, Alison E. Hipwell, Theodore J. Huppert, Robert T. Krafty
arxiv-2301-01373.description: Abstract With rapid development of techniques to measure brain activity and structure, statistical methods for analyzing modern brain-imaging play an important role in the advancement of science. Imaging data that measure brain function are usually multivariate time series and are heterogeneous across both imaging sources and subjects, which lead to various statistical and computational challenges.

arxiv-2304-13681.title: Ray Conditioning: Trading Photo-consistency for Photo-realism in Multi-view Image Generation
arxiv-2304-13681.creator: Eric Ming Chen, Sidhanth Holalkere, Ruyu Yan, Kai Zhang, Abe Davis
arxiv-2304-13681.description: Abstract Multi-view image generation attracts particular attention these days due to its promising 3D-related applications, e.g., image viewpoint editing. Most existing methods follow a paradigm where a 3D representation is first synthesized, and then rendered into 2D images to ensure photo-consistency across viewpoints.

arxiv-2311-10893.title: Towards consistent nuclear interactions from chiral Lagrangians I: The path-integral approach
arxiv-2311-10893.creator: H. Krebs, E. Epelbaum
arxiv-2311-10893.description: Abstract Low-energy nuclear interactions have been extensively studied in the framework of chiral effective field theory. The corresponding potentials have been worked out using dimensional regularization to evaluate ultraviolet divergent loop integrals. An additional cutoff is then introduced in the nuclear Schrödinger equation to calculate observables.

arxiv-2411-06307.title: Acoustic Volume Rendering for Neural Impulse Response Fields
arxiv-2411-06307.creator: Zitong Lan, Chenhao Zheng, Zhiwei Zheng, Mingmin Zhao
arxiv-2411-06307.description: Abstract Realistic audio synthesis that captures accurate acoustic phenomena is essential for creating immersive experiences in virtual and augmented reality. Synthesizing the sound received at any position relies on the estimation of impulse response (IR), which characterizes how sound propagates in one scene along different paths before arriving at the listener’s position.

arxiv-2412-18853.title: Generalized Turán problems for a matching and long cycles
arxiv-2412-18853.creator: Xiamiao Zhao, Mei Lu
arxiv-2412-18853.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xiamiao Zhao, Mei Lu. Let ℱ \mathscr{F} be a family of graphs. A graph G G is ℱ \mathscr{F} -free if G G does not contain any F ∈ ℱ F\in\mathcal{F} as a subgraph. The general Turán number, denoted by e ​ x ​ ( n , H , ℱ ) ex(n,H,\mathscr{F}) , is the maximum number of copies of H H in an n n -vertex ℱ \mathscr{F} -free graph.

arxiv-2508-00333.title: Tensor Elliptical Graphic Model
arxiv-2508-00333.creator: Jixuan Liu, Zhengke Lu, Le Zhou, Long Feng, Zhaojun Wang
arxiv-2508-00333.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jixuan Liu, Zhengke Lu, Le Zhou, Long Feng, Zhaojun Wang. We address the problem of robust estimation of sparse high dimensional tensor elliptical graphical model. Most of the research focus on tensor graphical model under normality.

arxiv-2512-22992.title: 𝒪 ⁡ ( α s 2 ​ α ) {\mathcal{O}(\alpha_{s}^{2}\alpha)} corrections to quark form factor Preprint:
arxiv-2512-22992.creator: Tanmoy Pati, Narayan Rana, V. Ravindran
arxiv-2512-22992.description: Abstract We present the analytic results for the non-singlet contributions to the three-loop mixed strong-electroweak 𝒪 ⁡ ( α s 2 ​ α ) {\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_{s}^{2}\alpha) virtual corrections to the quark form factors. The primary challenge of this computation arises from the presence of massive vector bosons within the loops.

arxiv-2601-10392.title: Multi-Temporal Frames Projection for Dynamic Processes Fusion in Fluorescence Microscopy Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2601-10392.creator: Hassan Eshkiki, Sarah Costa, Mostafa Mohammadpour, Farinaz Tanhaei, Christopher H. George, Fabio Caraffini
arxiv-2601-10392.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Hassan Eshkiki, Sarah Costa, Mostafa Mohammadpour, Farinaz Tanhaei, Christopher H. George, Fabio Caraffini. Fluorescence microscopy is widely employed for the analysis of living biological samples; however, the utility of the resulting recordings is frequently constrained by noise, temporal variability, and inconsistent visualisation of signals that oscillate over time. We present a unique computational framework that integrates information from multiple time-resolved frames into a single high-quality image, while preserving the underlying biological content of the original video.

cusick-sketches-six-nations-1827.title: David Cusick's Sketches of Ancient History of the Six Nations
cusick-sketches-six-nations-1827.creator: David Cusick
cusick-sketches-six-nations-1827.description: The Tuscarora historian's 1827 record of the Ot-ne-yar-heh, the Stone Giants — the foundational Native American 'wildman' tradition behind Sasquatch lore.

europmc-pmc3648782.creator: Colović MB, Krstić DZ, Lazarević-Pašti TD, Bondžić AM, Vasić VM.
europmc-pmc3648782.description: Acetylcholinesterase is involved in the termination of impulse transmission by rapid hydrolysis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine in numerous cholinergic pathways in the central and peripheral nervous systems. The enzyme inactivation, induced by various inhibitors, leads to...

pmc-11356876.title: The Concentration of Salivary Extracellular Vesicles Is Related to Obesity
pmc-11356876.creator: Kristin Röhrborn, Martin Krueger, Mirjam Kalusa, Simone A. Fietz, Alexander Ewe, Achim Aigner, Michael Stumvoll, Peter Kovacs, Matthias Blüher, Imke Schamarek, Kerstin Rohde-Zimmermann
pmc-11356876.description: Background and aims: Saliva is essential for the proper dilution and distribution of taste molecules on the tongue. It harbors extracellular vesicles (EVs), which mediate cell–cell communication. Changes in the composition of salivary EVs may arise under obese conditions and may potentially be involved in taste sensation and dysregulated eating behavior.

pmc-12470108.title: Transcriptome Analysis of Different Chinese Cabbage Varieties Under Cd and Pb Stresses
pmc-12470108.creator: Shiqi Peng, Hao Zhang, Junlei Wang, Liyuan Mu, Sijing Sun, Ao Li, Naiming Zhang, Li Bao, Ilya Vladimirovich Seregin, Anna D Kozhevnikova
pmc-12470108.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In recent years, soil heavy metal pollution has become increasingly serious, particularly Cd and Pb pollution, and heavy metals have been accumulating in soil–crop systems, posing great risks to human health. In this study, four Chinese cabbage varieties with different Cd and Pb accumulation traits were cultivated using hydroponics and transcriptome sequencing technology to reveal the response mechanism of Chinese cabbage to Cd and Pb stress at the molecular level.

pmc-12515340.title: Could the New Generation Mobile Base Stations Reduce the Nutritional Content of Primary Production Sector Products?
pmc-12515340.creator: Sotirios Maipas, Nikolaos Kavantzas
pmc-12515340.description: r. However, the situation becomes more complex when multiple antennas are present, making it more challenging to identify radiation-free areas. Readers should refer to the article by Nilsson and Hardell, 1 which presents a case study of a family experiencing the so-called “radiation syndrome” due to the presence of two 5G base stations directed toward their apartment.

pmc-12523217.title: Association between thoracic adiposity and survival in non-metastatic breast cancer
pmc-12523217.creator: Anlan Cao, Ijeamaka Anyene Fumagalli, Wendy Y. Chen, Adana A. M. Llanos, Charles P. Quesenberry, Bette J. Caan, Elizabeth M. Cespedes Feliciano
pmc-12523217.description: BackgroundTotal adiposity measured by abdominal computed tomography (CT) at the third lumbar vertebrae (L3) has been associated with breast cancer survival, but most patients undergo chest CT. If adipose tissues at the thoracic level, including those surrounding the thoracic organs, are associated with survival, they could be used to inform care for significantly more breast cancer patients.

pmc-13084788.title: Stem-like PD-1+TCF-1+ CD8+ T cells result from helpless priming and rely on CD4+ T-cell help to complete their cytotoxic effector differentiation
pmc-13084788.creator: Julia Busselaar, Douwe M T Bosma, Mo D Staal, Xin Lei, Yanling Xiao, Jannie Borst
pmc-13084788.description: BackgroundAntigen-specific CD8+ T cells can be in a stem-like programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1)+TCF-1+ differentiation state that progresses into terminal exhaustion in cancer and chronic infection. These stem-like cells are important, since they are the responders to PD-1 targeted immunotherapy and a potential resource for antitumor immunity.

pmc-13241767.title: Intramuscular hemangioma of the thoracic wall: Diagnostic challenge mimicking breast pathology—A case report
pmc-13241767.creator: Ma del Rosario García Calderón, Karina Pesce, Fernando Bañuelos Noriega, Lucia Alejandra Carrillo Calvo, Carolina Arroyo Zayas, Javier Cuevas Alvarado, Carolina Higuera Velázquez, Herman Isaac Tenorio Naranjo, Alberto Rubio Muñoz, Amador Ramírez
pmc-13241767.description: Intramuscular hemangiomas are uncommon benign vascular tumors, accounting for less than 1% of all hemangiomas, and are particularly rare in the thoracic wall. When originating from the pectoralis major muscle, they may clinically and radiologically mimic primary breast pathology, creating a diagnostic challenge.

pmc-13455298.title: Microbiome and metabolome patterns centered on cancer cachexia link skeletal muscle and adipose tissue depletion to clinical outcomes in locally advanced rectal cancer
pmc-13455298.creator: Zhixing Kuang, Qing Zhan, Jiannan Tu, Anchuan Li, Wei Guo, Rong Zheng, Hao Jiang, Benhua Xu
pmc-13455298.description: BackgroundCancer cachexia is a multifactorial syndrome characterized by involuntary weight loss and tissue wasting; it was associated with adverse survival outcomes in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). However, its biological basis and links to the gut microbiome, circulating metabolites, and body composition in LARC remain unclear.

uslaw-usc-t7-s1281.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 35 (Agricultural Adjustment Act Of 1938). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. This chapter may be cited as the “Agricultural Adjustment Act of 1938”.
